title: Endovascular therapy of thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysms: evolution of techniques and outcomes over time in a major vascular surgery centre
summary: In recent years, the treatment of aortic aneurysms has evolved through the increased use of minimally invasive procedures. Open surgery used to be the standard, but now endovascular techniques with special stents are becoming more and more important, especially for high-risk patients. Although this reduces mortality during surgery, there are still problems such as endoleaks, spinal ischemia and unclear long-term results. In addition, there are still knowledge gaps regarding optimal patient selection, treatment planning and long-term monitoring. This study examines how the treatment of jAAA and TAAA has evolved in a specialized center and its impact on short- and long-term outcomes.
conditions: Thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysm, without mention of rupture

interventions.name: This retrospective study analyses the endovascular treatment of thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysms in a large vascular surgery centre. The primary endpoint of this study is mortality (in-hospital mortality, 30-day mortality and all-cause mortality during follow-up).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
All patients who were treated endovascularly for jAAA or TAAA between 01.01.2007 and 31.12.2023 at the Department for Vascular and Endovascular Surgery
Exclusion criteria:
Age < 18 years
Open surgical interventions
